q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of solar modules assembled in India?
title: Solar module carbon footprint per watt
short: Add the bought-in cells, glass, aluminium frame, EVA, backsheet and junction box per module from supplier figures; cells are usually the largest share. Add the line's electricity for stringing, lamination and testing, then divide by watts produced.
audience: Solar module assemblers and their buyers

ul: Solar cells by watt, with the cell maker's figure and country.
Front glass, aluminium frame, EVA and backsheet by weight.
Junction box, cables, sealant and packing.
Laminators, the largest electricity load on the line.
Framing, curing, flash testing and EL inspection.

p: Report per watt peak, since module power ratings differ. Keep the cell origin with the figure.

example.title: Worked example: module line per watt (one month)
lines: Plant total: 213,000 / 50,000,000 = 0.00426 kg CO2 per watt
Add cells, glass, frame and backsheet for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
